$comment: Phase 0 seed — canonical phrasings library. Each entry is a topic with the 3+ phrases users have likely already absorbed from popular sources. The lint script (Phase 1) reads this to enforce the 'invisible familiarity' rule (lint 7.2.1): every Speakable's definition-equivalent beat must contain >= 1 anchor from this file for its topic. Every entry is tagged 'agent-seeded' per Plan §15B.1 — a future human pass refines them.

topics.title: Thread basics & lifecycle
phrasings: smallest unit of execution within a process
shares memory with the parent process
lifecycle states: New, Runnable, Running, Blocked/Waiting, Terminated

topics.title: Thread vs Runnable vs Callable
phrasings: Thread is a class, Runnable is an interface
Callable returns a value and can throw checked exceptions
Future holds the eventual result of a Callable

topics.title: Executor framework
phrasings: decouples task submission from thread management
fixed pool, cached pool, scheduled pool
shutdown vs shutdownNow

topics.title: Synchronization & locks
phrasings: intrinsic lock on the object's monitor
ReentrantLock with explicit lock and unlock
fairness costs throughput

topics.title: volatile vs atomic
phrasings: volatile guarantees visibility but not atomicity
AtomicInteger uses compare-and-swap under the hood
atomic operations avoid the lock entirely

topics.title: HashMap internals
phrasings: array of buckets
key-value pair
hashcode picks the bucket
collision resolution via chaining
treeify at bucket size 8 in Java 8+

topics.title: ArrayList vs LinkedList
phrasings: array under the hood vs nodes with pointers
fast read vs fast insert/delete
cache locality favours ArrayList

topics.title: HashSet & TreeMap
phrasings: HashSet is backed by a HashMap
TreeMap is a red-black tree giving sorted order
TreeMap operations are O(log n)

topics.title: equals & hashCode contract
phrasings: if equals returns true, hashcode must match
hashcode picks the bucket; equals picks the entry inside it
breaking the contract breaks every hash-based collection

topics.title: Comparable vs Comparator
phrasings: Comparable is the natural order on the class
Comparator is a separate strategy you can swap
compareTo returns negative, zero, or positive

topics.title: Generics & type erasure
phrasings: type parameters disappear at runtime
compile-time type safety only
you can't do new T() because T is gone at runtime

topics.title: Checked vs unchecked exceptions
phrasings: checked = compiler forces handling, RuntimeException = doesn't
checked is for recoverable conditions, unchecked for programmer errors
Error is a third bucket — JVM-level

topics.title: try-with-resources
phrasings: automatically closes anything that implements AutoCloseable
close runs in reverse order of declaration
suppresses close-time exceptions into the primary

topics.title: String immutability & String pool
phrasings: Strings are immutable in Java
the String pool interns string literals
intern() puts a runtime String into the pool

topics.title: == vs equals
phrasings: double-equals compares references, equals compares contents
two String literals share a pool reference
new String("a") is not double-equals to "a"

topics.title: OOP four pillars
phrasings: data plus the methods that work on that data
blueprint vs instance
Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, Abstraction

topics.title: Abstract class vs interface
phrasings: interface is pure contract, abstract class can mix in state
single inheritance for classes, multiple for interfaces
default methods since Java 8 narrowed the gap

topics.title: Inner classes
phrasings: static nested vs inner vs local vs anonymous
inner class holds a reference to the enclosing instance
lambdas replaced most anonymous-class use

topics.title: static & final keywords
phrasings: static belongs to the class, instance belongs to the object
final variable can't be reassigned after initialisation
final class can't be extended; final method can't be overridden

topics.title: Garbage collection generations
phrasings: young generation for short-lived objects
old generation for survivors that age out of young
minor GC vs major GC vs full GC

topics.title: JIT compilation
phrasings: interpreter to start, JIT compiles hot paths to native code
C1 (client) vs C2 (server) compilers
tiered compilation by default

topics.title: Reflection & annotations
phrasings: inspect classes, methods, fields at runtime
annotations are metadata read by reflection or processors
RetentionPolicy decides if annotation survives to runtime

topics.title: IoC & DI
phrasings: Inversion of Control hands wiring to the container
dependency injection puts collaborators in via constructor or setter
constructor injection is the modern default

topics.title: Spring bean lifecycle
phrasings: instantiate, populate, BeanPostProcessor before init, init method, ready, BeanPostProcessor after init
@PostConstruct runs after dependency injection
@PreDestroy runs on context close

topics.title: Spring bean scopes
phrasings: singleton (default) and prototype, plus web scopes (request, session, application)
singleton means one per ApplicationContext, not per JVM
prototype beans aren't managed for destruction

topics.title: @Component / @Service / @Repository / @Controller
phrasings: @Component is the catch-all stereotype
@Service for business logic, @Repository for persistence, @Controller for web
Spring scans them all the same way; the names express intent

topics.title: Spring AOP basics
phrasings: cross-cutting concerns like logging, security, transactions
proxy-based AOP via JDK or CGLIB
self-invocation bypasses the proxy

topics.title: @Transactional propagation & isolation
phrasings: REQUIRED joins the existing transaction or starts one
REQUIRES_NEW always starts a new one and suspends the old
isolation: READ_UNCOMMITTED, READ_COMMITTED, REPEATABLE_READ, SERIALIZABLE

topics.title: Spring Boot auto-configuration
phrasings: @EnableAutoConfiguration scans the classpath
starters bring in opinionated defaults
@ConditionalOnClass / @ConditionalOnProperty drive conditional bean wiring

topics.title: @RestController & @ResponseBody
phrasings: @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody on every method
Jackson serialises the return value to JSON
@RequestBody deserialises the request body

topics.title: Exception handling with @ControllerAdvice
phrasings: @ControllerAdvice catches exceptions across controllers
@ExceptionHandler maps an exception to a response
ResponseEntityExceptionHandler is the Spring base for REST

topics.title: Profiles & properties
phrasings: spring.profiles.active selects a profile
application-{profile}.yml gets layered on top of application.yml
@Profile guards beans by active profile

topics.title: Actuator endpoints
phrasings: /health, /info, /metrics, /env
expose them with management.endpoints.web.exposure.include
secure them or scope them to an internal port

topics.title: ACID properties
phrasings: Atomic — all or nothing
Consistent — invariants hold across boundaries
Isolated — concurrent transactions don't see each other's intermediate state
Durable — survives a crash

topics.title: SQL transaction isolation levels
phrasings: READ_UNCOMMITTED allows dirty reads
READ_COMMITTED prevents dirty reads but allows non-repeatable reads
REPEATABLE_READ prevents non-repeatable reads but allows phantoms
SERIALIZABLE prevents all of those

topics.title: JPA cascades
phrasings: CascadeType.PERSIST, MERGE, REMOVE, REFRESH, DETACH, ALL
cascade controls what happens to children when the parent is operated on
ALL is a footgun — REMOVE deletes children too

topics.title: Lazy vs eager loading
phrasings: lazy = fetch the relation when you touch it
eager = fetch it with the parent
lazy outside a transaction throws LazyInitializationException

topics.title: N+1 query problem
phrasings: one query for the parent list, N more for each child collection
fix with JOIN FETCH, entity graphs, or @BatchSize
the N comes from triggering the lazy loader inside a loop

topics.title: Indexing & EXPLAIN
phrasings: index turns a full scan into a B-tree lookup
EXPLAIN shows the query plan
covering index serves the read entirely from the index

topics.title: Connection pooling
phrasings: HikariCP is the modern default
more connections is not faster — they queue at the database
size the pool to roughly (cores * 2) + a small fudge for spindles

topics.title: Optimistic vs pessimistic locking
phrasings: optimistic checks a version on update; pessimistic locks the row up front
@Version field for JPA optimistic locking
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE for pessimistic

topics.title: REST principles
phrasings: stateless, uses HTTP verbs, resources via URLs
GET safe and idempotent, PUT idempotent, POST not
uniform interface, layered system

topics.title: Idempotency
phrasings: same request, same effect, no matter how many times
idempotency key in the request lets the server dedupe
GET, PUT, DELETE are idempotent by spec

topics.title: HTTP status codes
phrasings: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error
201 Created with Location header for new resources
204 No Content when there's no body to return

topics.title: API versioning
phrasings: URI versioning (/v1/...), header versioning, content-negotiation versioning
URI versioning is loud but easy to debug
deprecate versions on a published timeline

topics.title: Pagination patterns
phrasings: offset/limit (simple, slow on deep pages)
cursor-based (stable across inserts)
keyset for predictable performance

topics.title: JWT structure
phrasings: header.payload.signature, base64url-encoded
header carries the algorithm, payload carries the claims
signature proves the issuer with the key

topics.title: OAuth 2.0 flows
phrasings: Authorization Code with PKCE for browsers and native apps
Client Credentials for service-to-service
Resource Owner Password Credentials is deprecated

topics.title: Rate limiting
phrasings: token bucket and leaky bucket are the workhorses
fixed window and sliding window for HTTP-friendly headers
return 429 Too Many Requests

topics.title: Circuit breaker
phrasings: closed — open — half-open
trip when the failure rate crosses a threshold
half-open lets one request through to test recovery

topics.title: Kafka basics: partitions & consumer groups
phrasings: topic split into partitions for parallelism
one consumer per partition within a group
key chooses the partition (hash of key mod partitions)

topics.title: Exactly-once vs at-least-once delivery
phrasings: at-most-once may lose, at-least-once may duplicate, exactly-once needs idempotent processing
Kafka exactly-once via transactions and idempotent producers
deduplicate at the consumer with an idempotency table

topics.title: SOLID principles
phrasings: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
depend on abstractions, not concretions
open for extension, closed for modification

topics.title: Design patterns (classics)
phrasings: Singleton (one shared instance), Factory (delegated construction), Builder (fluent setup), Strategy (pluggable algorithm), Observer (publish-subscribe)
Gang-of-Four catalogue
patterns are vocabulary, not imports

topics.title: Composition over inheritance
phrasings: has-a versus is-a
composition gives you behaviour by holding it, inheritance by being it
favour interfaces and composition for flexibility

topics.title: Layered architecture
phrasings: presentation, application, domain, infrastructure
dependencies flow inward
each layer talks only to the one below

topics.title: Hexagonal / clean architecture
phrasings: ports and adapters
domain core knows nothing about frameworks
drive adapters in from the edge

topics.title: CQRS basics
phrasings: Command Query Responsibility Segregation
writes go through commands, reads through queries
two models so each can be optimised independently

topics.title: Event-driven design
phrasings: publish events, react to events
decouples producers from consumers
eventual consistency is the default

topics.title: DRY vs KISS
phrasings: Don't Repeat Yourself
Keep It Simple, Stupid
premature DRY couples; KISS keeps the seam

topics.title: Capacity estimation
phrasings: writes per second, reads per second, GB per day, peak factor
average vs peak — 5x is a common rule
year-out storage to size the partitioning

topics.title: FR vs NFR
phrasings: Functional requirements = what the system does
Non-functional = latency, availability, durability, security
NFRs constrain the architecture more than FRs

topics.title: CAP theorem & trade-offs
phrasings: Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance — pick two during a partition
CP refuses writes during a partition; AP accepts and reconciles later
PACELC extends CAP to the no-partition case

topics.title: Caching strategies
phrasings: cache-aside, read-through, write-through, write-back
TTL plus invalidation handle staleness
watch out for cache stampede and hot keys

topics.title: Load balancing
phrasings: round-robin, least-connections, IP hash, weighted
L4 vs L7 — transport vs application layer
health checks remove unhealthy backends

topics.title: Sharding & replication
phrasings: shard for write scale, replicate for read scale and HA
consistent hashing reduces re-shuffling on resize
read replicas drift; the leader is the source of truth

topics.title: URL shortener design
phrasings: base-62 short keys
Redis or in-memory cache fronting the store
30 to 50 to 1 read-to-write ratio is typical

topics.title: Rate limiter design
phrasings: token bucket for steady allowance, sliding window for HTTP-shaped traffic
Redis is the usual store for distributed counters
return 429 with Retry-After

topics.title: News feed design
phrasings: fan-out-on-write for normal users, fan-out-on-read for celebrities
feed cache per user with paginated retrieval
the celebrity problem is the bottleneck

topics.title: Authentication vs authorization
phrasings: authentication = who you are; authorization = what you can do
AuthN runs before AuthZ in the request lifecycle
MFA strengthens authentication; RBAC structures authorization

topics.title: OAuth 2.0 flows (detail)
phrasings: Authorization Code with PKCE for browsers and native apps
Client Credentials for service-to-service
the access token is a bearer credential — treat it like a password

topics.title: JWT signing
phrasings: HS256 is symmetric (shared secret); RS256 is asymmetric (private/public)
asymmetric keeps the signing key off the verifier
rotate keys with a kid header and a JWKS endpoint

topics.title: CSRF & XSS
phrasings: CSRF tricks the browser into making an authenticated request
XSS injects script into the page
CSRF token plus SameSite cookies; XSS prevented by output encoding and CSP

topics.title: Password hashing (bcrypt)
phrasings: bcrypt with a tunable work factor
argon2 is the newer recommendation
salt prevents rainbow tables; pepper adds a server-side secret

topics.title: TLS handshake
phrasings: ClientHello with cipher suites, ServerHello with chosen suite plus certificate
key exchange via ECDHE for forward secrecy, then Finished messages
TLS 1.3 collapses the handshake to one round trip

topics.title: Test pyramid
phrasings: lots of unit tests, fewer integration tests, very few end-to-end tests
fast feedback at the bottom, fidelity at the top
ice-cream cone is the anti-pattern (top-heavy)

topics.title: Unit vs integration vs contract test
phrasings: unit tests one class with collaborators mocked
integration tests cross a process boundary
contract tests assert the API both sides agree on

topics.title: Mocking vs stubbing
phrasings: mock = verify how it was called
stub = canned answers, no verification
fake = working implementation, lighter than the real one

topics.title: Code coverage
phrasings: line, branch, condition coverage
high coverage doesn't mean high quality
use it as a smoke detector, not a target

topics.title: TDD basics
phrasings: red, green, refactor
the test drives the design
small steps; never let red sit

topics.title: CI/CD pipeline stages
phrasings: build, test, package, deploy
fail fast at the cheapest stage
secrets out of the source, into the secret store

topics.title: Docker layers & multi-stage builds
phrasings: each Dockerfile instruction is a cached layer
multi-stage = build in one image, run in a slim one
order layers by churn — least-churning at the bottom

topics.title: Kubernetes pod & service
phrasings: pod = one or more containers sharing network and storage
service = stable virtual IP fronting a set of pods
ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer types

topics.title: Blue-green & canary deployments
phrasings: blue-green: two full environments; switch the router
canary: a small slice of traffic to the new version first
automate the rollback on SLO regression

topics.title: Rolling updates
phrasings: replace pods a few at a time
maxSurge and maxUnavailable bound the disruption
readiness probes gate traffic during the swap

topics.title: Region vs AZ
phrasings: region = geographic; AZ = isolated datacenter inside a region
deploy across AZs for HA, across regions for DR
cross-AZ traffic is cheap; cross-region is not

topics.title: IAM basics
phrasings: users, groups, roles, policies
least privilege by default
role assumption for cross-account access

topics.title: S3 consistency model
phrasings: strong read-after-write consistency for new objects (since 2020)
list operations may briefly lag
eventual consistency for overwrites was the old model

topics.title: Autoscaling
phrasings: horizontal (more instances) vs vertical (bigger ones)
scale on a leading metric (CPU, queue depth, custom)
cooldown prevents flapping

topics.title: VPC & networking basics
phrasings: VPC = isolated virtual network
subnets are AZ-scoped; route tables direct traffic
NAT gateway for outbound from private subnets, IGW for public

topics.title: Log levels & structured logging
phrasings: ERROR for actionable, WARN for unusual, INFO for milestones, DEBUG for diagnosis
structured = JSON with named fields, not a printf line
MDC propagates a correlation ID across the whole request

topics.title: Distributed tracing
phrasings: trace = the whole request, span = one hop
OpenTelemetry is the vendor-neutral standard
context propagated via the traceparent header

topics.title: SLI / SLO / SLA
phrasings: SLI = the measurement, SLO = the internal target, SLA = the customer contract
error budget = 1 minus the SLO, spent on risk
exhausting the budget means freeze releases until it refills

topics.title: Error budget
phrasings: remaining permissible unreliability for the period
burn rate alerts when consumption is faster than refill
spent budget means slow change down until it refills

topics.title: Incident response & runbooks
phrasings: declare, page on-call, establish a commander, branch into investigation and customer comms
runbook gives the first 5 steps without thinking
the longer on-call sits without one, the more value the runbook returns

topics.title: Post-mortem & RCA
phrasings: blameless culture, 5-whys, contributing factors, action items with owners
what went well, what went poorly, where we got lucky
publish to the team — quiet post-mortems don't change behaviour

topics.title: STAR method
phrasings: Situation, Task, Action, Result, plus Reflection
structure prevents rambling; depth comes from the action
specifics over generalities — names, numbers, weeks

topics.title: Self-introduction
phrasings: name, current role, two or three highlights, what's drawing me to this role
30 to 60 seconds, not 3 minutes
land on a hook the interviewer can pick up

topics.title: Conflict resolution
phrasings: name the disagreement, describe the other side's want, describe my move toward shared ground, describe the outcome
the value is the move toward, not winning the argument
always end with what I'd do the same and what I'd do differently

topics.title: Failure & learning
phrasings: pick a real failure, own the part you owned, name what you'd do differently
specific, recent, with stakes
rehearsed but not canned

topics.title: Weakness question
phrasings: name a real weakness, name what I'm doing about it, name the early signs of progress
no fake-strength weaknesses
the move toward improvement is the answer
